LRU translation cache key ignores the fallback chain it now depends on

With fallbacks enabled, the value returned for (key, locale) depends on the fallback chain, which depends on SiteSetting.default_locale and on which fallback locales happen to be loaded at lookup time. The cache key is only key + config.locale + backend object_id, and nothing in this change invalidates entries when default_locale changes or when a fallback locale is loaded later. The first computed value, including a 'translation missing' string that is frozen and cached at line 75, is then served until LRU eviction (300 entries) or reload!.

No specs cover the new fallback behavior or the load path

This change affects global translation behavior: a new fallback chain, the fallback backend module included globally, pluralization moved from pluralization.rb into this file, config.i18n.fallbacks removed from three environment files, and a new ensure_loaded! path in set_locale and the accelerator. The PR adds no specs. Nothing verifies that a key missing in a non-English locale resolves through the site default and then :en, that the fallback works when the fallback locale has not been loaded (the gap described in translate_accelerator.rb line 68), or that pluralization still works after the include was moved. A unit test for FallbackLocaleList#[] and a request spec exercising set_locale with a missing key would catch these regressions.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation

The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in this change is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java, and no no-arg overload exists in the class hierarchy. The `services` module will not compile, so the whole PR (including all the new tests) cannot build or run. The intended call is presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which is already non-null inside this branch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

false_positives.candidate:
Negative webauthn-button check uses catch(Exception), so it can pass vacuously

In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (and again around line 312), the absence of the webauthn form is checked with `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any Exception thrown while looking up the element, such as a WebDriverException from a stale or not-yet-loaded page, is swallowed and the check passes without verifying anything. The same PR and file already use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` for this kind of check, which only accepts the expected exception.

Re-auth skip is disabled for every user whenever passkeys are enabled in the realm

The shortcut that skips the username form during re-authentication is now bypassed for any user as soon as passkeys are enabled for the realm, regardless of whether that particular user has a passkey. A password-only user re-authenticating with prompt=login in a passkey-enabled realm is now shown the username page and must submit it, where previously they were skipped. The only new UsernameForm re-auth test uses a passkey-only user, so this regression for password-only users is not covered. If the intent is to only show the form when the user can use a passkey, the condition should check the user's passkey credentials rather than only the realm flag.

Unused PasswordCredentialModel import added by this PR

The import `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` is added in this PR, but nothing in the file references it (the new tests only use string/nullValue checks). It should be removed to keep the build's unused-import checks clean.

Unused import NoSuchElementException left behind

The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` uses were replaced by `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)` in this PR, so the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is now unused. This can fail a checkstyle or unused-import check in the build.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offset is passed straight into a queryset slice, which Django rejects

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is the raw negative offset and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices and raises an error, so the request returns a 500. The branch that is supposed to reach data beyond normal pagination bounds therefore never returns data. A user can reach this with any crafted cursor string whose offset is negative, provided the advanced flag is set.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member is dereferenced without a None check

RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional, since a requester may not be a member of the organization. The expression `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` only avoids the dereference when the user is a superuser. For any other requester with no membership record, this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Whether OrganizationAuditPermission guarantees membership for non-superusers is not visible in this diff, so this needs a None guard or a confirmed invariant.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to a datetime, crashing any non-empty page

The endpoint sends `order_by="-datetime"` to this paginator, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime` for each AuditLogEntry. `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` raise TypeError on a datetime. `build_cursor` calls this key function on the results, so with `optimized_pagination=true` every organization that has at least one audit entry gets a 500. Only the empty-result case avoids the call. DateTimePaginator.get_item_key avoids this by converting the datetime to a millisecond epoch value. This class did not copy that logic, so it cannot serve its only use case. Subclassing DateTimePaginator or porting its conversion would fix it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Comment claims a Cursor behavior change that the diff does not make

The added comment says the Cursor now 'allows negative offsets ... enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets'. The code line below it, `self.offset = int(offset)`, is unchanged. The class already accepted negative offsets, and nothing in the change makes pagination more efficient. The comment documents a nonexistent optimization and should be removed.

Comments justify exposing data beyond pagination bounds on the claim that queryset-level checks exist, which is false

The comments at lines 878-879 say the negative-offset branch 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' and that this 'is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'. The queryset here is only filtered by organization_id (organization_auditlogs.py line 48). The role check that enables the mode is in the endpoint (line 71). Nothing checks permissions at the queryset level. The intent is a privilege-gated path that widens what an admin can reach, and its safety argument is wrong and unreviewed. The branch should be removed or its authorization model explicitly designed and documented.

Negative offsets are silently clamped to 0 in BasePaginator for every paginator, not only the new one

The change to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` affects BasePaginator.get_result, which DateTimePaginator, Paginator and every other cursor paginator inherit. It is not gated by the new query parameter. Before this change, a non-prev cursor with a negative offset (reachable through Cursor.from_string) raised a slicing error. Now it silently returns the first page with a cursor built from the original negative offset. The comment at lines 179-181 says negative offsets are being allowed, but the code does the opposite, clamping them. The comment and the global behavior change both need to be reconsidered, and the change should be separated from this feature.

New paginator, query-parameter path and negative-offset behavior change have no tests

The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, a new `optimized_pagination` branch in the endpoint, an advanced-features gate, and a global change to BasePaginator offset handling, but adds no tests. The first basic use (one page of audit entries with the param set) crashes, as described in the get_item_key and value_from_cursor findings. A simple endpoint test would have caught it. Tests are also needed for the default DateTimePaginator path, which the BasePaginator change now affects.

PR description is a placeholder and the 'performance' framing is unsupported

The description is only 'Test 1', so nothing explains why the endpoint gets an undocumented `optimized_pagination` query parameter or who it is for. The code comments at lines 68-75 call this a performance optimization, but the optimized branch issues the same ORM queries as DateTimePaginator (its only real difference is the broken negative-offset branch), and no measurements are included. The title and comments overstate what the change does.

Privileged mode is gated on the raw is_superuser flag rather than an active superuser session

The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` directly. Sentry's superuser pattern normally checks an elevated, session-scoped superuser state (for example via is_active_superuser(request)). Using the raw user flag can grant the advanced mode to a superuser who has not elevated in this session. The impact is limited while the advanced path is broken, but the gate should follow the codebase's superuser convention.

value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then bound against a DateTimeField

DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor converts the millisecond cursor value back into a timezone-aware datetime. This class returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` then appends that int to the `extra(where=...)` params against `auditlogentry.datetime`, so any request carrying a next/prev cursor either fails at the database (timestamp compared with integer) or fails Django's DateTimeField validation. Pagination past the first page cannot work on this path.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset branch relies on Django negative slicing, which is unsupported

When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative indices ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so this raises instead of returning data. The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false, and the claim 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is unsupported. Any admin request with a crafted cursor carrying a negative offset gets a 500, and the feature the branch advertises does not work.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Previous-page cursor with negative offset still passes a negative start index to queryset slicing

For is_prev cursors, start_offset is set to the raw offset, which Cursor.from_string allows to be negative from user input. The slice queryset[start_offset:stop] then raises on a negative index, so a user-supplied cursor such as '0:-1:1' produces a 500. The crash predates this PR, but the PR adds a comment at lines 179-181 calling this behavior safe and intentional, and clamps only the next-page direction, so the inconsistency is now written down as design.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys (auditlog optimized_pagination path)

The auditlog endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the raw attribute value. That attribute is a datetime, so math.floor raises TypeError. build_cursor calls key(results[0]) whenever cursor.value is 0 and there are results, so the first page of any superuser or global-access request with optimized_pagination=true and at least one audit log returns a 500. value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset would compare against a datetime column on later pages. The paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style handling (strftime/timestamp conversion) or the endpoint must not route datetime keys to it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Comment claims a negative-offset feature that this change does not implement

The added comment says Cursor now allows negative offsets for advanced pagination and enables reverse pagination from arbitrary positions. The diff changes nothing in this constructor (self.offset = int(offset) is unchanged), and the paginators that consume negative offsets crash on them. The comment describes behavior that does not exist, so it should be removed or corrected.

Hard key access on end_timestamp_precise can fail an entire batch

val['end_timestamp_precise'] is a strict lookup, and the cast(SpanEvent, ...) is type-only and does not validate anything at runtime. Before this PR the field was not read. A single message missing it raises KeyError inside process_batch, which fails the whole batch and can leave the consumer retrying the same poison batch. Use val.get with a fallback, or validate and skip the bad message with a metric.

Key type change from Redis set to sorted set breaks in-flight buffers during deploy

The span-buf:s:* keys change from SET to ZSET but keep the same name prefix. Any segment key written by the old code is a SET. After deploy, ZADD in process_spans, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, and ZSCAN in _load_segment_data all fail with WRONGTYPE. Ingestion raises for those traces, and flush_segments raises before done_flush_segments runs, so the queue entries are not cleared until the keys expire (redis_ttl, default 3600s). The PR needs a new key prefix or a drain/migration plan.

Module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as sets

The glossary says span-buf:s:* are 'the actual set keys', but after this PR they are sorted sets (ZADD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, ZPOPMIN). Update the docstring so future readers do not assume SET commands.

No test covers the new 1000-span eviction, the set-to-zset change, or the redirect depth change

The headline feature of this PR, evicting spans beyond 1000 during insert, has no test. The added lines only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures, so nothing checks that the segment is capped, that the oldest spans are the ones evicted, that merges keep the right scores, or that the loop limit behaves as intended. Add tests that insert more than 1000 spans through process_spans and assert the resulting count and which payloads survive.

Redirect-chain depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 and caveat comment removed

The loop bound changed from 10000 to 1000 with no mention in the PR description, and the comment explaining the limit's consequence was deleted. Redirect chains deeper than 1000 are now cut off silently, so their spans are attached to an intermediate segment rather than the root. Either keep the old limit or document the change and keep the caveat.

Span eviction at 1000 is silent: no log or metric when spans are dropped

When span_count exceeds 1000, zpopmin silently removes the lowest-scored (oldest by end timestamp) spans from the segment. The Python side previously logged 'Skipping too large segment' and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded, and that guard was removed in buffer.py. Dropped spans are now invisible to operators, and the limit is hardcoded here rather than configured. Emit a metric (and ideally a log) from the script or the caller when eviction occurs.

Unrelated pagination changes and an undocumented query parameter are bundled into a spans PR

The PR title is about span buffer eviction, but this file, paginator.py, and cursors.py add an experimental audit-log paginator switch. That switch is an undocumented optimized_pagination query parameter, and the PR description is just 'Test 2', so reviewers have no rationale for it. Split these changes into their own PR with a description, or revert them from this one.

ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregation, doubling scores of duplicate payloads

zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE, so the default SUM applies. When the same payload already exists in the destination (for example a redelivered Kafka message, or a span present in both merged sets), its score becomes the sum of the two end timestamps. That corrupts the eviction ordering, which relies on score = end_timestamp_precise. Use AGGREGATE MIN or MAX so the score is preserved.

max_segment_spans config is now dead and disagrees with the hardcoded Lua limit

After this PR the span-count check in _load_segment_data was removed, so the max_segment_spans constructor argument (default 1001) is never read. The effective limit is the hardcoded 1000 in add-buffer.lua. Configuration that appears to control the limit no longer does, and the two defaults disagree. Remove the parameter or wire it into the script.

optimized_pagination path is untested and crashes on the first page

The new branch gated by optimized_pagination=true has no test. Such a test would immediately expose the datetime TypeError in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key, so the endpoint's new path is broken and unverified. Add a test for a superuser request with that parameter and at least one audit log entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the request dataset, not the dataset actually queried

The check passes the request-level dataset, but the query runs against scoped_dataset, which differs in the dashboard split path (discover for the errors-only and transactions-only sub-queries). The errors/transactions/discover guard in _should_apply_sample_weight_transform is therefore evaluated for the wrong dataset. The split path requires metrics_enhanced, so the outer dataset is always a metrics dataset there. The guard returns False and the errors-only discover sub-query is never upsampled, while the same query outside the split path would be. The decision should be made from the dataset the query actually runs on.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Allowlist check and cache write run before the dataset gate

On every cache miss, _are_all_projects_error_upsampled runs options.get and cache.set, even for spans, metrics, and transactions queries. The dataset check on line 40 then discards the result. The cache get and set happen on every _get_event_stats call. Checking the dataset and request gate first, then returning early, would avoid the Redis round trips and the option lookup for queries that can never be upsampled.

Allowlist option read via options.get with no registration in the diff

The allowlist comes only from options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []). None of the eight changed files registers this key in the options defaults. Sentry's options manager raises an UnknownOption error for unregistered keys, so on a cache miss _are_all_projects_error_upsampled would raise. That call happens in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects before any dataset gating, so every events-stats request with a project could fail, not only error queries. The tests patch options in this module, so the real lookup never runs and CI would not catch it. Register the option or confirm it already exists.

Bare except blocks silently ignore malformed sample rates

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps dict access and float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass'. A malformed client_sample_rate is silently dropped and the event is stored without sample_rate. This helper runs inside store_event, which many tests use, so a bad test payload gives no signal. The try around a plain dict .get chain is unnecessary. Validation should be explicit or errors should surface.

Comments claim caching and consistency that the code does not provide

The comments say the cached result 'ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and that storing the decision 'allows for better query optimization and caching'. Nothing is cached at this point. The decision is recomputed on every _get_event_stats call, and the underlying eligibility is a 60-second cache in error_upsampling.py. Calls within one request can therefore disagree if the cache entry expires between them. The comments should be corrected.

Equations containing count() are not upsampled alongside the rewritten yAxis

Only the exact count() entries in query_columns are rewritten. Equations passed through equations=self.get_equation_list(...) are not transformed, so an equation such as equation|count() * 2 returns un-upsampled values while the plain count() yAxis returns upsampled values in the same response. The inconsistency is not handled or documented.

Query-classification and cache paths are untested

test_is_error_focused_query and test_should_apply_sample_weight_transform only check the exact strings 'event.type:error' and 'event.type:transaction'. Nothing covers negated filters ('!event.type:error'), compound queries, or 'event.type:errors', which is exactly where the substring check goes wrong. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects itself is not tested, so the cache hit and miss paths and the dataset gate are unverified. The endpoint tests also never exercise the topEvents or RPC branches where the transform is applied.

Stray file committed at repository root

A regular file named sentry-repo containing 'Subproject commit a5d29095...' is added at the repository root. It is not a real gitlink and appears to be an accidental artifact that pins the base commit. It should not be part of this change and should be removed from the PR.

Substring match classifies negated and compound event.type filters as error queries

The check 'event.type:error' in query is a substring test. Queries such as '!event.type:error', 'event.type:errors', or '(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)' all return True. For those queries the count is rewritten to sum(sample_weight), but non-error rows have no sample_weight, so the sum drops them and the count is wrong (for '!event.type:error' it can come out as 0). The filter should be parsed as a token rather than matched as a substring. No test covers negation or compound queries.

Transform is not gated on metrics or on-demand routing

The count() rewrite to upsampled_count() is applied regardless of use_metrics, has_metrics, use_metrics_layer, or on_demand_metrics_enabled, which can route a discover-dataset query to a metrics or on-demand builder. upsampled_count is registered only in discover.py's function converter, so in those routes the function would not resolve, or the query would silently fall back to a non-upsampled count. The transform should be gated on the builder actually used.

Unrelated change to an existing error message

The topEvents validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This has nothing to do with upsampling and is not mentioned in the PR. Any client matching the exact string will see a change. It should be split out or called out in the description.

Upsampling branch in the RPC path is unreachable

use_rpc is true only when dataset is spans_rpc or ourlogs. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False for both, so upsampling_enabled is always False when this block runs. The block is dead code, and it gives the false impression that RPC datasets get upsampled. Remove it, or rework the gating if RPC upsampling was intended.

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code, so allowlist changes are only picked up after 60s

invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called in the diff, and no allowlist write path invokes it. Its docstring says it should be called when the allowlist changes, but nothing does. An allowlist change therefore takes up to 60 seconds to affect upsampling, because of the cache.set at line 38. Either wire it to the option update path or remove it and correct the docstring.

sum(sample_weight) silently drops events that lack a weight

sum() ignores NULLs, so any error event without a sample_weight contributes 0 instead of 1 to upsampled_count. This includes events ingested before the rollout and events with no client sample rate. The docstring in error_upsampling.py (lines 85-86) says no null handling is needed because the schema guarantees the column, but nothing in the diff enforces that. Time ranges spanning the rollout would silently undercount for allowlisted projects. The fallback for a missing weight should be defined explicitly, for example coalesce(sample_weight, 1).

upsampled_count is a public aggregate with a different result type from count()

The function is registered without private=True, so users can request upsampled_count() in any discover query, including transaction queries the upsampling guard is meant to exclude. Its default_result_type is 'number' while count() is 'integer', so the field type reported in meta changes for upsampled responses. Either mark it private or document and validate the new public aggregate and its result type.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error IDs are paired with nodestore results by position, not by key

nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a mapping keyed by node id that omits missing nodes, and its order is not guaranteed to match error_ids. zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs each error id with whatever value comes next in the mapping. When any error's nodestore entry is missing (for example after retention expiry), every later error gets the title, message and timestamp of a different event. The 'data is not None' filter runs after the misalignment, so it does not prevent this. Each id should be looked up in the returned mapping.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged table path renders hard-coded empty data and ignores query results

When the use-table-widget-visualization flag is enabled, each table widget is replaced by TableWidgetVisualization with columns set to an empty array and tableData hard-coded to empty data. This ignores tableResults, loading, result.meta, the custom field renderer and minTableColumnWidth. Any organization with the flag sees empty tables for every table widget. This looks like scaffolding and should not ship in this form.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation no longer requires timestamp or age; truthiness checks skip 0 values

The previous dataclass required timestamp, but both age and timestamp are now optional, so a report with neither field validates. The mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness on initial_data, so age 0 or timestamp 0 combined with the other field is accepted. The checks should test for key presence and the presence of one field should be required.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag gate

analytics.record runs before features.has(...). Requests from organizations without the preprod-artifact-assemble feature, which receive a 404, still emit preprod_artifact.api.assemble events. This pollutes the metric with traffic from non-enrolled orgs. The record call should move below the feature check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
Analytics event name changed, breaking continuity of the View HTML metric

The trackAnalytics call for the View HTML click was renamed from replay.view_html to replay.view-html. Existing dashboards and queries keyed on the old name will stop receiving data for this action. The rename should be noted, or the old name kept for continuity.

Comment points to a replacement migration that is not part of this change

The no-op body says the correct migration is 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, but no such file appears in the changed files. 0917 and 0920 are both replaced with no-ops, and the 0917 test is deleted. If the replacement is not in this PR, org-level saved searches will never be converted into GroupSearchView rows, and the comment misleads readers. Either add the replacement or correct the reference.

Default autofix tuning changed from low to off for every project without an explicit setting

Changing DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT (and the matching projectoptions default) to off changes live behavior for every project that never set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning, with no migration, backfill or release note. The tests were only updated to match the new default. This should be called out explicitly or handled with a data migration.

Environment filter silently dropped from the attribute keys request

The previous useTraceItemAttributeKeys sent environment: selection.environments to the trace-items attributes endpoint. The new makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits it and says it is intentionally unsupported, which contradicts the prior behavior. Attribute keys from every environment are now returned, which is a silent behavior change.

Every paginated page's Seer summary includes all error events of the replay

The endpoint paginates over recording segments and calls analyze_recording_segments once per page, passing the replay-wide error_events list each time. gen_request_data restarts error_idx at 0 for every page, and this trailing loop yields every error not yet consumed. Each page's Seer request therefore contains every error in the replay, including errors whose timestamps fall in other pages, so the same errors are repeated across page summaries. The new tests only exercise a single page with one error, so they pass despite this.

Exceptions from blob deletes are silently discarded

pool.map returns a lazy iterator and its result is never consumed, so any exception raised by storage_kv.delete other than NotFound is never re-raised. The with-block only waits for completion. A failed blob delete (permissions, network error) produces no log or metric, and delete_replays then archives the replay anyway, leaving orphaned recording blobs with no trace. Consume the results (for example list(pool.map(...))) or submit futures and check their exceptions. This is pre-existing, but it is in a file this PR touches.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is only applied when a search query is entered

The early return when searchQuery is empty returns the sorted list without applying the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter. The filter only runs when the user types a search. With the default empty search, is_segment, project_id and received are shown, but they disappear as soon as any search is typed. The hidden-attribute rule should apply in both cases.

Recommended event is loaded from nodestore for every issue in every PR comment

get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() and then get_environment() for each of up to five issues per comment. Each call does a nodestore fetch and a DB lookup, and this runs on every PR comment build. The environment could be fetched in a batch, or cached per issue.

Snuba query and nodestore fetch run on every page request, even when error context is disabled

The endpoint runs query_replay_instance and fetch_error_details before paginate, so both run on every paginated request, not once per replay. The Snuba query also runs when enable_error_context=false, where its result is discarded except for error_ids that are then ignored. Error details should be fetched once per replay or skipped when disabled.

Summary card renders with empty content when the API returns no summary

useFeedbackSummary returns summary as string or null. tooFewFeedbacks is only true when numFeedbacksUsed is 0 and success is false. If feedbacks were used but the LLM call failed (success false, summary null), this component still renders the 'Feedback Summary' header with an empty paragraph. The component should return null when summary is null.

Title truncation and environment formatting have no test coverage

The new _truncate_title path (titles longer than 50 characters get an ellipsis) and the non-empty environment suffix in get_environment_info are not exercised by the GitHub or GitLab PR comment tests. The existing tests use short titles and only check the happy path. A regression in truncation or the environment suffix would not be caught.

Unescaped issue title is placed inside a markdown link in PR comments

The template renders '[**{title}**]({url})' with the raw issue title. Titles derive from error messages, which can be influenced by application input. A title containing ']' followed by '(' closes the link text early and lets the remaining text form an arbitrary link destination in a comment the Sentry bot posts on the PR. The environment name is also interpolated raw inside backticks. The title should be escaped or sanitized before interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is an unlocked read-modify-write, allowing double use and restoration of spent codes

The code is read and checked at lines 139-145, then the entire array is rewritten at line 149 with no transaction, lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent logins using the same code can both pass indexOf before either write lands, so one backup code can be spent twice. Concurrent logins with different codes also race: each writes back its own copy of the array, so the later write can restore a code the other request already nulled. Use an atomic compare-and-swap on the stored value (or a transaction with row locking) so that consumption is single-use.

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Plaintext backup codes and blob URL persist in component state after the dialog closes

resetState() clears password and step but not backupCodes or backupCodesUrl. After the dialog is closed, the plaintext recovery codes stay in React state, and the blob URL that encodes them is never revoked on close (it is only revoked on the next setup call). Clear the codes and revoke the URL when the dialog closes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup codes stored reversibly instead of hashed

Backup codes are stored with symmetricEncrypt, so anyone holding CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, or a DB dump together with that key, can recover every unused code and log in as the user. These codes are bearer secrets. Because they are random and high-entropy, a one-way hash (for example SHA-256 with a comparison on the submitted code) would suffice and remove this exposure. Severity is low because the same key already protects TOTP secrets.

Closing the backup-codes step via X/Escape/overlay skips the Close handler and loses the codes

During DisplayBackupCodes the Dialog's onOpenChange is passed straight through, so the close X, Escape, and overlay click bypass the Close button's handler. By this point the enable request has already succeeded and 2FA is active on the server. onEnable() is never called, so the parent is not told 2FA is enabled, and the codes are discarded with no way to view them again. No regenerate endpoint exists in this PR. Route dismissals during this step through the same handler as the Close button, or block them until the codes have been acknowledged.

Copy button shows success toast without awaiting or handling clipboard failure

navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast fires unconditionally. On insecure origins or when permission is denied, the write fails (or navigator.clipboard is undefined and throws), yet the user is told 'Backup codes copied!'. Await the promise and show an error toast on failure.

Enable test asserts on a switch behind the open backup-codes dialog, with a known-vacuous assertion left in place

The PR adds a FIXME stating that this assertion 'passes even when switch is not checked'. The enable test also never closes the backup-codes dialog that now sits on top of the page, so the switch is checked behind the modal. The assertion is therefore weak and knowingly so. Close the dialog and assert data-state='checked' as the disable test does, rather than shipping a check the author has already identified as not validating anything.

No test covers logging in with a backup code, the core new behavior

The TODO defers backup-code login testing, but this is the main user-facing addition of the PR (the 'Lost access' flow). Nothing exercises the authorize() backup-code branch, the consumption of a code, rejection of reuse, or the new error messages. The disable-endpoint backup path is also untested. At minimum, add an e2e test that logs in with a code, confirms it is accepted once, and confirms reuse is rejected.

Non-string backupCode from JSON body throws an unhandled TypeError

req.body.backupCode is taken from a JSON body without type checking. Any truthy non-string value (number, object, array) makes .replaceAll throw, which escapes the handler as an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of a JSON error. Check typeof req.body.backupCode === 'string' before normalizing it.

Password check skipped whenever totpCode is non-empty, which also bypasses it for the new backup-code path

The password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`, so any non-empty totpCode skips the password check entirely. The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever credentials.backupCode is non-empty, regardless of totpCode. A request with a valid email, a valid backup code, and any non-empty totpCode (for example 'x') logs in without the password ever being verified. Backup codes are meant to replace only the second factor, but this turns them into a single-factor credential (email plus a 40-bit code). The same gap already exists for TOTP, but this PR adds a new route that depends on it. Password verification should not be skippable by supplying an unrelated second-factor field.

Users who reach 2FA via Google/SAML cannot use backup codes at all

When 2FA is triggered after an OAuth/SAML sign-in (totpEmail set), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only has a Cancel button, so the 'Lost access' toggle is never rendered. Even if the UI were reachable, authorize() in next-auth-options.ts (lines 113-115) throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled for non-CAL users when totpCode is empty, so a backupCode-only submission is always rejected for these users. Users who sign in with Google or SAML and lose their authenticator therefore have no recovery path on the login page. Either wire backup codes into the external TOTP flow or state this limitation explicitly.

missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such action exists

The message says 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' No UI in this PR generates codes outside the initial setup, and the setup endpoint refuses to run once 2FA is enabled. Users who enabled 2FA before this change (backupCodes null) are shown this message on login and sent to a screen where they cannot act. Their only path is disabling 2FA with a TOTP code and re-enabling it. Reword the message or add a regenerate action.

tabIndex -1 on the password show/hide toggle removes it from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField

This change is unrelated to backup codes and is not mentioned in the PR description, but it applies to every PasswordField in the app. tabIndex={-1} removes the visibility toggle from the Tab order, so keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they typed. The button has only an sr-only label, so it is effectively unreachable without a pointer. This is an accessibility regression. If the goal was only to skip the toggle on the login form, handle it at that call site instead.

type="password" passed to PasswordField overrides its computed type, so the show/hide toggle does nothing

PasswordField renders type={isPasswordVisible ? 'text' : 'password'} and then spreads {...props} afterward. The type='password' passed here wins, so the input never switches to text. Clicking the eye toggle changes the icon and label but the value stays hidden. This was previously a plain TextField; the swap introduces a dead control on the enable-2FA password step. Drop the explicit type prop.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
CalDAV reports success when no event was written for a team member

The filter keeps only calendars whose externalId equals the first destination's externalId. For a team member's CalDAV account that URL does not exist, so the filtered list is empty. `responses` is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the function returns a uid as if the event was created. CalendarManager records success=true, the member never gets the event, and no error is logged.

Destinations without credentialId lose their externalId and can create duplicate events

For destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the destination's externalId. The result therefore has `externalId` undefined, and the booking reference is stored with a null externalCalendarId. Google picks its calendar only by credentialId, so the event goes to 'primary' and later update/delete cannot find the right calendar. The previous code stored `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In addition, this loop runs once per destination against the same list of credentials of that type, so N such destinations and K credentials produce N×K events.

Error logging removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block

The `console.error(message)` call was removed. The catch now returns fallback results with success=false and emits no log, so calendar update failures disappear silently. The `message` string is still built but never output.

Hangout patch still uses selectedCalendar, which can now be undefined

The insert now falls back with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `events.patch` (line 168) still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`. That value is undefined when no destination matches the credentialId, so the patch is sent without a calendarId. The patch is fire-and-forget with no callback or catch, so the failure is unhandled and the hangout link description is silently not updated. Use the same fallback in the patch.

No tests cover the new multi-destination create/update/cancel logic

The PR states no tests were added. The new multi-destination logic in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, and the Google calendar-id selection, are where most of the defects above sit (null-calendar regressions, dead predicates, lost credentialIds). A unit test per destination shape (with and without credentialId, empty and multiple destinations) would catch these.

Organization relation dropped from dynamic-group user query without explanation

The `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection was removed from the dynamic-user query. The PR does not explain why or add a replacement. If any downstream code in this handler reads `users[i].organization` for dynamic group bookings, it now receives undefined. The removal should be justified or reverted.

Per-destination calendar is only honored by the Google service; other calendar apps still use the organizer's calendar

CalendarManager calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. The destination externalId is only attached to the returned result, so the calendar implementation never sees which calendar this credential should write to. Only the Google service resolves its calendar by credentialId. Lark (googlecalendar-style `destinationCalendar[0]` at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 129), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 75) and CalDAV (lib/CalendarService.ts line 161) always use the first destination, which for a collective event is usually the organizer's calendar. A team member's Lark or O365 credential therefore targets the organizer's calendar ID with the member's token, which fails. The collective-event fix works only for Google.

Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each instance

The PR changed the top-level logic to iterate over all calendar references, but this recurring-cancel path still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)`, so only the first calendar reference per instance is considered. For a collective recurring booking with a second calendar reference (for example the team member's), that event is never deleted. The calls go to every calendar credential with the first reference's uid, which fails silently for the other accounts.

Recurring deletions are repeated once per calendar reference

This block sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. Each iteration re-runs the same deletion of every updated booking across all calendar credentials. With two calendar references and a recurring series, each instance's event is deleted twice (or more), producing duplicate API calls and duplicate entries in `apiDeletes`. The deletion should run once, outside the loop.

Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer and event type have no destination calendar

`destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (around line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so every collective member's calendar is discarded. This is the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The array may also start with a team member's calendar, which the calendar services then treat as the organizer's main calendar.

Video references are saved without credentialId

The `credentialId` mapping in `create()` was changed to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Now every video reference is stored with a null credentialId. handleCancelBooking.ts only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (around line 491), so cancelled bookings leave the Zoom/Daily/etc. meeting behind. The seated-cancellation video update path has the same dependency. Restore `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without a breaking-change note

The event object is sent as-is in BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED webhook payloads (`...evt` in sendPayload). `destinationCalendar` changes from a DestinationCalendar object (or null) to an array (or null here, [] in other paths). Existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was edited to expect `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED while still expecting `null` for BOOKING_CREATED, so the payload is now inconsistent across events and the contract change is undocumented.

deleteEvent fallback never finds the destination calendar and defaults to primary

Same dead predicate as in updateEvent: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. `calendarId` then becomes 'primary' (line 322), so cancelling a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId deletes from the user's primary calendar, not the calendar the event was created on, and the event remains on the destination calendar.

loadUsers error handling turns client errors into 500s and leaks Prisma messages

The new try/catch wraps the whole user-loading path. The `dynamicUserList` validation at line 728 throws a plain Error, which is not an HttpError, so it is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users', losing the message and the 4xx status. Conversely, Prisma known-request errors are rethrown as HttpError 400 with the raw Prisma message, which exposes internal details. The old code let these errors propagate unchanged.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'

When a refresh response has no refresh_token, this writes the placeholder string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data. Callers persist that value: Office365 (CalendarService.ts line 264) spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credential, overwriting the valid refresh token with 'refresh_token'. The next refresh then sends a bogus token and fails with invalid_grant. In sync mode the minimum schema always drops refresh_token, so every sync refresh replaces it. Leave the field undefined and keep the existing refresh token instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync-mode schema computes keys from z.string().toString(), dropping every field except access_token

z.string().toString() is a constant (Object's toString, '[object Object]'), not a key pattern, so both computed keys collapse into one property and the second (z.unknown().optional()) overrides the first. The schema therefore validates only access_token. Zod strips unknown keys by default, so when sync is enabled (line 16) expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and other fields are removed from .data. Callers then compute with undefined: Zoom computes expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined*1000 (NaN, serialized to null, which makes zoomTokenSchema reject the stored key); Zoom and Google also persist the refresh_token placeholder; Salesforce saves a key without instance_url; Office365 keeps its old expires_in and refreshes on every call. The intended 'any numeric property is expiry' needs passthrough or a different shape.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh stores the safeParse wrapper instead of the parsed tokens

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result ({ success, data }), not the parsed data. Here that wrapper is assigned to `key` and written to credential.key on every token refresh, regardless of whether sync is enabled. The stored key becomes { success: true, data: {...} }. On the next call, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) in googleAuth (line 75) finds no top-level access_token/refresh_token and throws, so Google Calendar stops working for that user after the first hourly refresh. Other callers (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) correctly read .success/.data. Return or store `.data` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response that callers do not expect, and status is never checked

When sync is enabled the function returns the fetch Response from the self-hoster's endpoint, while the non-sync branch returns whatever refreshFunction returns. Callers are written against the latter: Google reads res?.data (line 94 of googlecalendar CalendarService), and a fetch Response has no .data, so token.access_token throws. The catch swallows that and the stale access token is used silently. zoho-bigin and zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error / .data.expiryDate on the result and throw TypeError. Hubspot treats it as a token object. Also response.ok is not checked, so a 500 HTML page is passed on as if it were tokens, and there is no timeout, so a hung endpoint blocks every calendar or video call for that user. Zoho Bigin passes the credential id as the Cal.com userId to the sync endpoint

refreshAccessToken receives credentialId (credential.id, the row id) and forwards it as the 3rd argument of refreshOAuthTokens, which is the userId and is sent to the self-hoster's endpoint as calcomUserId. In sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens of user <credential row id>, which is not necessarily the credential's owner. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText === 'OK' instead of response.ok

statusText is the HTTP reason phrase. It is not defined for HTTP/2 responses and is often empty, so a successful refresh can be rejected. The thrown HttpError also reports statusText with a fixed 400 regardless of the real status, and the response body (which contains Salesforce's error_description) is never read. Invalid payloads and undecryptable keys surface as unhandled 500s

appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on malformed input (line 31). symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse (lines 57-59) throw on a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext. None are caught, so the caller gets a 500 with a stack trace in logs instead of a 400, and a self-hoster's retry logic will treat client errors as server failures. Concurrent deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same user and app

The handler does findFirst (line 62) then create (line 83) with no transaction or lock. Two deliveries for the same user and app can both see no row and both create one, unless the schema has a unique constraint on (userId, appId), which this PR does not add. Later lookups that take the first matching credential may then pick a row that is not the one just synced.

The comment says the endpoint should return only the access token and expiry date, but callers read more. Google reads expiry_date. Hubspot reads expiresIn. Zoom, Webex and Office365 video read expires_in, and Office365 video stores the whole response as the credential key. Lark parses a {code, data} envelope and needs refresh_token and refresh_expires_in. Following the comment gives NaN expiry, or in Office365 video expiry_date = now (line 84), which forces a sync call on every request, and loses refresh tokens. The actual contract (field names, units, envelope) should be documented, for example next to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in .env.example (line 240, currently undocumented). The PR description also says docs are required, but none are included.

Helper both throws on failure and returns a SafeParse result, so callers' .success checks are dead

On schema failure this throws, yet on success it returns the safeParse wrapper. Callers that check `!parsed.success` (Zoom VideoApiAdapter around line 108, Salesforce around line 92) can never reach that branch, and the error text is generic. Office365 previously logged the provider's response on schema failure; that logging was removed in this PR, so the provider error is now lost. Pick one contract: return the parsed data or throw.

In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn is then undefined, so expiryDate becomes NaN (line 192), and line 198 stores the Response instance as the credential key. A Response does not carry the token fields as enumerable properties, so the stored key either becomes an empty or garbage object (losing accessToken and refreshToken) or the update fails. The catch at lines 203-205 only logs, so nothing surfaces. The HubspotToken annotation on line 177 hides the mismatch from the type checker.

No tests for the webhook, the sync refresh path, or the schema helper

The PR adds a webhook that writes credentials, a refresh indirection touching about twelve integrations, and a new schema helper, and the PR description says no tests were added. Several defects above (wrapper stored as the key, stripped fields, placeholder refresh token, wrong userId, missing prisma import) would be caught by unit tests of parseRefreshTokenResponse and refreshOAuthTokens with sync on and off, and by webhook tests for auth, validation and create/update.

Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it

The new refresh code calls prisma.credential.update (line 96), but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a TypeScript compile error, and at runtime constructing the client throws a ReferenceError, so every Salesforce calendar operation (contact search, event creation, availability) fails for all users. Add the import.

Salesforce refreshes its token on every client construction, bypassing the sync endpoint

getClient now posts to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row on every CalendarService construction, even when the stored access token is still valid. Each calendar operation therefore costs an extra network round trip and a DB write, and concurrent operations each refresh and overwrite the same row. The refresh also goes directly to Salesforce with the Cal.com consumer secret and does not use refreshOAuthTokens, so with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set Salesforce still refreshes on its own, contrary to the sync design. Refresh only when the token is expired and route it through refreshOAuthTokens.

Sync update leaves a credential flagged invalid even after fresh tokens arrive

Refresh failure paths set invalid: true on the credential (for example googlecalendar CalendarService lines 112-118 on invalid_grant, and Webex/Zoom invalidateCredential). The update branch here only writes key (lines 73-80), so after the self-hoster pushes fresh tokens the credential stays flagged invalid and remains unusable in code paths that check the flag. Clear invalid on update.

Webhook secret compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison

The shared webhook secret is checked with plain string inequality, which short-circuits at the first differing byte and leaks timing information. For an authentication check on a network endpoint, compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers (for example, hash both values first).

Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the Zoom app slug is 'zoom'

Zoom credentials are created with appId 'zoom' (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts line 73), and the webhook resolves app slugs the same way. Here refreshOAuthTokens is called with 'zoomvideo', the directory name rather than the app slug. A self-hoster's sync endpoint keyed on appSlug will not recognize it or will look up the wrong app. Use 'zoom'.

The new value is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at line 48, not read from the database at write time. If two cron invocations overlap, or the row changes between read and write, increments are lost (both read 0 and both write 1), so the retry limit can be exceeded. The same pattern appears at line 184. Prisma's `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in the database.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unscoped deleteMany hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1

The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` or `scheduled: false` filter. It hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount above 1, whatever its channel (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) and whether it is already scheduled. Only the SMS path writes retryCount today, so the immediate impact is small, but the predicate is broader than the feature described and will silently delete rows for any future channel that uses the counter. There is also an edge case: if Twilio accepts a message but the follow-up update to scheduled:true throws, the row stays scheduled:false, its retryCount can reach 2, and it gets deleted while the Twilio message is still pending. Cancellation via referenceId can then no longer find it. The clause should be scoped to `method: SMS, scheduled: false`.

false_positives.candidate:
Comment no longer describes what the deleteMany does

The comment says it deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed. The query now also deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or date, and it deletes unscheduled rows too. The comment is misleading for anyone maintaining the cleanup logic. It should describe both conditions.

Empty message or missing recipient is never counted as a failed attempt

The retry increments only happen inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. When the message resolves to empty, or the recipient is null (an SMS_NUMBER step with no sendTo, or a booking with no smsReminderNumber), nothing is scheduled and retryCount is not incremented. Such a reminder is re-attempted on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That unbounded retry is the behaviour this PR is meant to stop, so these cases should count as failures too.

Generated Prisma-derived artifacts may not be regenerated

Adding a column to WorkflowReminder changes what the generators in this schema emit (the kysely generator writes to ../kysely/types.ts and the zod generator writes to ./zod). The PR touches only schema.prisma and the migration. If those generated files are committed in this repository, they are now stale: typed queries will lack retryCount, and any drift check in CI will fail. No tests for the new retry and deletion behaviour

The PR changes deletion semantics and adds retry bookkeeping in three places (the failed-schedule branch, the catch block, and the deleteMany), but adds no tests. Coverage should include: a failed schedule increments retryCount; a reminder with retryCount 2 is deleted on the next run; a successful schedule does not increment retryCount; and the deletion is scoped correctly. Without tests, the off-by-one around `gt: 1` and the scoping problems above are easy to get wrong.

Transient provider errors permanently drop reminders after two attempts

Every failure consumes the retry budget equally: a falsy return from twilio.scheduleSMS (lines 178-186) and any exception (lines 189-199). The code does not distinguish permanent errors (e.g. invalid phone number) from transient ones (Twilio outage, rate limiting, network timeout). Two failures in consecutive cron runs cause the deleteMany at line 38 to remove the reminder permanently. The deletion is not logged and the user is not told. A brief provider blip is enough to lose reminders for every booking in the window. Consider backing off, counting only permanent error types, or at least logging each deletion.

Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole batch

The catch block now performs a prisma.workflowReminder.update (retryCount) with no try/catch. If that update throws, the exception escapes the for-loop, so the remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the handler rejects. One concrete trigger: a reminder deleted between the findMany and this point (for example by a booking cancellation or a concurrent cron run) makes Prisma throw P2025, and that is not handled. A transient DB error has the same effect. Before this PR the catch block only logged, so this is a new failure mode. Guard the update, or make per-reminder error handling non-throwing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

Cancellation flag write is fire-and-forget, so the reminder's fate is not guaranteed

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is async, but it is called without `await` here (and the same pattern appears in bookings.tsx line 490 and workflows.tsx). The `cancelled: true` UPDATE that now decides whether the reminder is sent may not complete before the handler returns, and on a serverless runtime the process can be frozen after the response. Errors are swallowed inside the helper's try/catch, so a failed write leaves the booking cancelled with no record that its reminder must be stopped, and nothing retries it. true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Immediate cancel path reuses the call that hits SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation cap

The `immediateDelete` branch sends `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. The PR description identifies this exact mechanism as the root cause: each cancelled send stays pending until its scheduled date, and once 100 are pending new cancels fail while the emails are still sent. This branch is used for rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts line 968), workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521), which can cancel many reminders at once. When the cap is hit, the error is swallowed by the catch at the bottom of the function, so the reminders are silently still sent. The branch also returns without touching the DB row, so the reminder keeps `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch until its scheduled date passes. If `CRON_API_KEY` is not configured and the request has neither an `authorization` header nor an `apiKey` query parameter, `apiKey` is `undefined` and the check `process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey` evaluates to `undefined !== undefined`, which is false, so the request proceeds. This is pre-existing, but the endpoint now also cancels SendGrid sends and deletes reminder rows, so an unauthenticated caller on a misconfigured deployment can trigger those side effects. The handler should reject when the key is missing.

New cancel-and-delete cron logic and cancelled flag have no tests

The PR changes cancellation semantics across handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking and workflows.tsx, adds a `cancelled` column with a migration, and adds a cron branch that calls SendGrid and deletes rows. None of this is covered by a test in the diff. The previous fix shipped broken with the failure silently swallowed. At minimum, tests should cover: a cancelled reminder inside the one-hour window being cancelled and deleted; a SendGrid failure for one reminder not blocking the others; and a paid booking's reminders being cancelled.

One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all deletes

The loop awaits `client.request` for every cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If any call throws (for example SendGrid rejects a batch that was already sent or already cancelled), the catch at lines 75-77 runs and the loop is abandoned, so the remaining reminders in the window are never cancelled. Also, `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a lazy PrismaPromise that only executes when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74. Because that await is never reached after an error, the deletes for reminders already cancelled earlier in the loop never run either. Those rows keep `cancelled: true`, and the next cron run (about 15 minutes later) hits the same failing reminder first. A single bad batch therefore blocks cancellation of every other reminder in its one-hour window, and emails for cancelled bookings still go out. Each cancel should be isolated (try/catch per reminder), and the delete should be awaited right after its own successful cancel.

Paid-booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled

For a paid booking the handler takes the `bookingToDelete.paid` branch (starts at line 363), refunds, sets status REJECTED, and returns at this line. The workflow reminder cancellation block (lines 484-493) and the zapier `cancelScheduledJobs` call come after this return, so they never run for paid bookings. The booking is cancelled, but its scheduled BEFORE_EVENT email and SMS reminders are still sent, which is the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. The same gap exists at line 437 (`return null` when the payment service is not implemented), and any throw between the status update at line 255 and line 484 leaves reminders uncancelled. Reminder cancellation should happen before the paid branch, or be duplicated into it.

SMS reminder row is only deleted if the Twilio cancel succeeds

The Prisma `workflowReminder.delete` runs after `twilio.cancelSMS` in the same try block. If Twilio throws (for example because the message is already sent or no longer cancellable), the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Before this change the callers deleted the row regardless of the Twilio result, so this is a regression: the row keeps `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`. The row deletion should not depend on the external cancel succeeding.

Unrelated UI restructuring bundled into a reminder-cancellation fix

The condition changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` and the phone block is unwrapped. This changes rendering for SMS_ATTENDEE steps, which no longer get an empty padded container. Nothing in the PR description or title mentions this UI change, and it is unrelated to cancelling reminders. It should be split into its own PR or described explicitly.
