Inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` the item context is the member User object, not the group, so `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves `automatic` against the user and is always falsy. The remove link therefore appears for automatic groups too. The server rejects those removals with a 422, and `removeMember` in the admin controller and model has no failure handler, so the click appears to do nothing. The flag needs to come from the controller or be passed into the item view.

create ignores alias_level even though the client now sends it

`Discourse.Group#asJSON` now includes `alias_level`, and the new-group form shows the alias-level selector. `create` assigns only name and visible, so the chosen alias_level is silently dropped and the group gets the default. The PR rewrote `create` but left this gap in place.

Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding

`group.users.delete(user_id)` with an integer id makes Rails 4 look the record up with `find` on the association, which raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound when that user is not a member. The old PATCH path tolerated removing non-members, and the deleted spec ('succeeds silently when removing non-members') asserted that. A double-click or a stale member list now produces a 404 that the Ember client does not handle.

limit/offset are unvalidated: negative values cause a 500, and limit has no cap

`limit` and `offset` come straight from `params.to_i`. A negative `limit` produces `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request fails with a 500; a negative offset fails the same way. There is also no upper bound on limit, so a single request can pull the full membership of any visible group. Clamp limit to a sane range and floor offset at 0.

GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from an array to an object

The endpoint now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` instead of a bare array of users, and the default page size changed. Any other consumer of this public JSON endpoint (plugins, API clients) will break silently. The PR description does not mention the contract change.

Admin update silently resets visible for clients using the old nested params

`update` now reads flat top-level params and no longer reads `group[...]`, and the PATCH membership path is removed. A client still sending the old nested payload (`group[name]`, `group[visible]`) gets `params[:visible]` nil, so `group.visible` is set to false without any error. The name change is also silently skipped.

No positive test for updating a non-automatic group

The `.update` context only checks that renaming an automatic group is ignored. The rename, visible, and alias_level paths for normal groups, which are the main behavior of the rewritten `update` action, have no test. The old test covering name changes for regular groups was removed.

New public members endpoint and its pagination have no spec

The `members` action changed its response shape, default limit, and query logic, and the group members UI now depends on the meta fields. No spec in this PR exercises pagination, meta values, the 50-member default, or access to hidden groups through `find_group`.

Stale selector targets the user-selector id that this PR renamed

`input#group-users` still sets a 600px width, but group.hbs now passes `id="user-selector"`, so this rule no longer matches anything. The layout rule is dead and the input falls back to the generic width.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist match counter is inflated because the check writes from inside validation

`should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the row, but it is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every `valid?` or `save` of a User whose email changed. In `UsersController#create` the code calls `user.valid?` (line ~168) and then `user.save` (line ~172), so one blocked signup attempt increments `match_count` twice, and any other validation call adds more. The statistic therefore does not reflect the number of blocked attempts. Also, a validator that mutates blocklist state couples every model using `validates :email, email: true` to that side effect. Record the match once in the controller or a single save path, and keep validation read-only.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same underlying architectural flaw: the blocklist checking method (`should_block?` / `should_block_email?`) has a write side effect (updating statistics/match count) during what should be a read-only check.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so case variants bypass a blocked address

`should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive match. Nothing normalizes the address first: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim, and the domain restriction in the same validator is case-insensitive (`Regexp.new(..., true)`). If 'spam@example.com' is blocked, a signup with 'Spam@Example.com' passes validation and is stored. The unique index on blocked_emails is also case-sensitive, so case variants can coexist as separate entries. Normalize both the stored value and the lookup key (for example with Email.downcase, which the codebase already uses for lookups).
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is case-sensitive, which allows users to bypass the blocklist by varying the case of their email address.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-atomic read-modify-write loses match_count increments under concurrency

`record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the count into Ruby, increments it, and writes it back. Two concurrent signup attempts that read the same value both write value+1, so an increment is lost. `save` also reruns validations, including the uniqueness query, just to bump a counter. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` or `update_counters`.

rejectedEmails is never cleared, so any server email error blocks that address until reload

Every response with `errors.email` pushes the address into `rejectedEmails`, and `emailValidation` then fails that exact address (line 69) for the controller's lifetime. That includes errors that are not about the blocklist, such as 'has already been taken'. The field then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` reason for an address that is well-formed but registered, and submit stays disabled for it even if the server-side condition changes (for example, an admin removes the blocklist entry). Consider clearing the list when the email changes or limiting it to the blocked-email error.

New errors and values keys in the failed-signup response have no spec

The failed-create JSON now includes `errors` and `values`, and the new client code depends on that shape (`result.errors.email && result.values`). No request or controller spec in this PR checks these keys, so renaming or dropping them would silently break the rejected-email handling in the frontend.

Moved domain whitelist/blacklist logic and the real blocklist path are untested here

The whitelist and blacklist checks were moved from User into EmailValidator in this PR, but this spec only covers the blocked-email branch, and it stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the real lookup is never exercised. Nothing in this PR checks the domain restrictions through the new validator, the short-circuit (no blocklist lookup once a domain error is added), or case-insensitive matching. Regressions in the moved logic or the case-sensitivity issue would not be caught by these specs.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items property

`-ms-align-items` is not a property in any browser's CSS. The declaration is silently dropped, so it does nothing, and it misleads readers into thinking an IE-specific alignment declaration is being emitted. The IE10 equivalent is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already on line 120. The line should be removed.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies that `-ms-align-items` is a non-existent CSS property and notes that the correct IE legacy property is `-ms-flex-align`, which is the exact same issue described in the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Bullet badges in topic title lose their top offset and inherit a new line-height

The diff deletes the `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule and adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. Bullet badges have no line-height of their own, so they now inherit 1.5 and lose the 5px top margin. Both changes shift where bullet category badges sit in the topic title. The PR does not mention either change, and nothing in this diff makes `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container that would justify a vertical-alignment change. This is an unexplained visual regression.

small-action becomes a flex row without sizing the description, and floats stop working

`.small-action` is now `display:flex`, but `.small-action-desc` gets no `flex-grow`/`flex: 1`. It therefore sizes to its content rather than filling the row. The old `padding-left: 4em` that reserved room for the avatar is replaced by `0 1.5%`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` is a no-op and, if the `button` is a direct child (the `button` selector at this nesting level suggests it is), `button { float: right }` at line 309 no longer pushes it to the right edge. The message box will not fill the post width and the button placement will change. This needs a visual check; as written it looks like an unverified layout change.

order(2) has no effect unless an ancestor of .extra-info-wrapper is a flex container

`order` only affects children of a flex or box container. This PR does not turn any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` into a flex container, so the new `@include order(2)` is dead CSS unless an ancestor is already flex in the base stylesheet or markup. The author should confirm that the rule does something or drop it.

Title claims a performance optimization; description is placeholder and scope is undocumented

The PR title says it optimizes header layout performance, but a float-to-flexbox layout change makes no performance measurement and the diff does not explain any performance gain. The description is only 'Test 5'. The diff also changes topic posts (`.small-action`), topic titles (`.extra-info-wrapper`, the removed bullet margin, the new line-height) and category badges, none of which are part of the header. Reviewers have no rationale for these visual changes and no before/after evidence. The description should state the scope, the intended visual changes and how they were verified.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users

`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`) the raw website URL is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, and `include_website_name?` only checks `website.present?`, so it is serialized for those users. It contains the host and, when the host matches the forum, the full path, so the restricted URL is effectively exposed again. This defeats the anti-spam restriction the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism exists to enforce. Fix: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list, or gate `include_website_name?` on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover website_name

The 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec checks that bio, location, website and profile/card background are not serialized. The new `website_name` attribute is not in this list, so the spec does not catch the leak where a TL0 user's website host and path are serialized to anonymous viewers. Add `website_name` to this list and make the untrusted check cover it.

Trailing slash on same-domain website is shown as 'example.com/'

For a website such as `http://example.com/` on a forum at `example.com`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so `website_name` becomes `"example.com/"`. Users who type a bare domain with a trailing slash will see a stray slash that the previous client-side `split('/')[2]` logic did not produce. Consider stripping a bare `/` path, for example by treating a path of `/` as empty.

Domain comparison is case-sensitive

`URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. A website entered as `http://Example.com/user` on a forum at `example.com` fails the `==` test on line 141 and falls through to the else branch. The result is `Example.com` with no path, so the feature silently does not apply. Downcase both hosts before comparing, including in the `ends_with?` and sibling comparisons.

Sibling-domain heuristic treats different registrable domains as the same site

The branch on line 146 compares everything after the first label. For a forum at `y.co.uk` and a website at `x.co.uk/page`, both have three labels and the comparison yields `co.uk == co.uk`, so the full path is shown as if the website belonged to the forum's site. The heuristic does not account for public suffixes such as `co.uk` or `github.io`. The result is misleading display text for unrelated sites, not a security issue, but it does not match the stated intent of the feature.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open is used on an admin-supplied URL

`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open. In Ruby 2.x, a string beginning with `|` is executed as a shell command rather than fetched. The setting is admin-only, so the exposure is limited, but the call should be explicit. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (open-uri) so only HTTP(S) fetches are possible.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify a security vulnerability in the exact same call `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. While the golden comment describes the issue as SSRF (fetching arbitrary internal or external URLs) and the candidate focuses on OS command injection via Ruby's `Kernel#open` (and suggests restricting to HTTP(S) fetches), they both point to the exact same unvalidated/unsafe `open` call on the `feed_polling_url` setting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring matching, so a prefix origin is accepted

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison. Any sender whose origin is a prefix of the forum URL passes. With `discourseUrl = "https://community.example.com/"`, a page served from the registrable domain `https://community.example.co` has an origin that is a prefix, so `indexOf` returns 0 and the message is accepted. The handler also never checks `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`. The practical effect is that a lookalike site can resize the iframe, but the check is wrong. Compare the exact origin (scheme, host, port) of `discourseUrl` with `e.origin`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same vulnerability: the origin check uses `indexOf` (substring matching) instead of exact origin comparison, allowing attackers with a malicious/lookalike domain to bypass the check.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
X-Frame-Options 'ALLOWALL' is not a valid value and is ignored by browsers

Valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unknown values, so this header does nothing; framing is permitted only because the browser ignores it. It also overwrites any X-Frame-Options set earlier in the request. If the intent is to allow framing from the configured host, use `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` with the embeddable host and remove this header.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the security vulnerability caused by setting 'X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL', which effectively disables clickjacking protection and allows unrestricted framing by overwriting previous headers. Although the golden comment also points out flaws in the surrounding referer validation, the core issue regarding the unsafe X-Frame-Options header is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Imported-from footer interpolates the URL into HTML without escaping The footer is built as `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The URL comes from the feed link or id and is inserted unescaped into a body stored as raw HTML. A link such as `http://x.test/'>` injects markup. The URL check on line 11 uses `^`, which matches after any newline, so the scheme check is also weaker than intended. Escape the URL before interpolating it, and anchor the scheme check at the start of the string.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment actually combines two issues: a NoMethodError when `contents` is nil, and an XSS vulnerability from unescaped `url` interpolation in the HTML. The candidate issue specifically and accurately identifies the second part of the golden comment (the XSS vulnerability due to unescaped URL interpolation in the footer link).

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dangling `if` modifier in `<%- end if %>` makes the embed template invalid

`<%- end if %>` closes the `if` opened on line 2 but leaves a stray `if` modifier with no condition. Once ERB compiles this, the result is not valid Ruby (the modifier is followed by the compiler's statement separator), so the `best` template fails whenever it is rendered. The intent is clearly `<%- end %>`. This breaks the main embed page for every request that finds an existing topic. The controller specs do not catch it because they never render views (no `render_views`), so a view or request spec is needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same syntax error in the ERB template: using `end if` instead of `end`, which results in invalid Ruby code that will fail when rendered.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One bad feed item aborts the whole poll, and nil content raises NoMethodError

The `rss.items.each` loop has no per-item error handling. `i.content` can be nil for feed items that only supply a description, so `i.content.scrub` on line 35 raises NoMethodError. `i.title` can also be nil. `TopicEmbed.import` can raise too, for example when the URL exceeds 255 characters, or when the embed's post has been deleted. Any of these aborts the loop, and the job has `retry: false`, so nothing retries. The next hourly run reaches the same item and fails again, so every item after it is never imported. Guard nil content and title, and rescue and log errors per item.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies that `i.content` can be nil for feed items that only supply a description, which causes `i.content.scrub` to raise a NoMethodError (nil pointer exception), matching the core issue described in the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Feed content is double-unescaped and stored as raw HTML, giving stored XSS on the forum

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` decodes entities that SimpleRSS has already decoded from the XML, so text meant to be shown literally (for example `&lt;img onerror=...&gt;` in the feed) becomes live markup. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates the post with `cook_method: raw_html` (topic_embed.rb:22). `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb:133), which skips the Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` unescaped (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), and the same cooked HTML appears in the forum topic. A feed item containing a script or event-handler payload therefore runs on the forum origin for every visitor, including staff. Feed content is third-party data, so this crosses a trust boundary. Run imported content through the normal sanitizer before storing raw HTML, and remove the extra unescape.

PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an outer transaction that has not committed

`TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator#create` calls `enqueue_jobs` (which triggers `process_post` and `feature_topic_users`) before the outer transaction commits. PostCreator's own comment says jobs must be enqueued after the transaction because workers may start on uncommitted data. With Sidekiq, a `process_post` job can run before the post and the TopicEmbed row are visible, find nothing, or fail, so the post is never processed (oneboxes, image sizes, and so on). Enqueue after the outermost commit, or do not wrap the creator in an outer transaction.

Anonymous requests can force unlimited outbound fetches and full feed polls

For any unknown `embed_url`, each request enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job without checking the host (the controller only checks the referer). The only throttle is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` in topic_retriever.rb:26-28, which runs inside the worker and is keyed on the exact URL string. An attacker can vary a query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key causes an outbound HTTP fetch of the embeddable host, and when feed polling is enabled it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (topic_retriever.rb:41), which downloads and re-imports the entire feed. Nothing rate-limits the endpoint, so this is a cheap way to exhaust outbound bandwidth and Sidekiq capacity. Validate the host in the controller before enqueueing, throttle per normalized URL in the request path, and do not run a full feed poll from a request-driven job.

`force: true` on a new table migration drops any existing topic_embeds table

`create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops an existing `topic_embeds` table before creating it. A migration that creates a new table gains nothing from this option and makes it destructive: running it in an environment where the table already exists (a partially migrated database, or another branch that created the table) silently deletes every embed-to-topic mapping. The importer depends on those mappings to avoid duplicate topics. Remove `force: true`.

Unrelated migration gains `force: true`, which drops existing top_topics data if rerun

This change adds `force: true` to the `top_topics` table creation. It is unrelated to embedding. If the migration runs in an environment where `top_topics` already exists with data, the table and all its counters are dropped. If the schema needs changing, add a new migration instead of editing one that may already have run.

setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a throttle key with no TTL

`$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire` are two separate commands. If the process dies or the connection drops between them, `retrieved:<url>` persists with no TTL. Non-staff users are then permanently throttled for that URL and it is never retried. Use one atomic command, `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

Missing post for an existing embed causes NoMethodError on update

`post = embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. When the content hash differs, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`. The stale embed row is never repaired, and in PollFeed this exception aborts the whole loop (poll_feed.rb:31), so every later item is skipped. Handle a missing post explicitly, for example by recreating the post or removing the stale embed.

Readability attribute whitelist does not restrict URL schemes

`attributes: %w[href src]` limits which attribute names survive, but it does not check URL schemes. A `<a href="javascript:...">` from the fetched page can survive into the body. That body is stored as raw_html (cook_method), so the link runs script on the forum when clicked. The source is the configured embeddable host, so exploiting this needs that site to be compromised or malicious, but the forum should not accept unsanitized HTML from it. Pass the output through the normal sanitizer with an allowed-scheme list.

embed_url is varchar(255) with no length check, so long URLs fail at insert

`t.string :embed_url` creates varchar(255) in PostgreSQL. The value comes from unauthenticated request params (embed_controller.rb:9) and from feed links, and nothing checks its length. A longer URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise StatementInvalid after the page has been fetched and the post built. The transaction rolls back, and every retry fails the same way. Validate the length at the controller and model, or use a text column.

Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the entire posts table

On PostgreSQL releases before 11, `add_column` with a default and `null: false` rewrites the whole posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum, reads and writes to posts are blocked for the duration. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL constraint, or schedule the downtime explicitly.

The --category option is silently removed from the Disqus import CLI

Removing `method_option :category` means `thor disqus:import --category X` now fails with an unknown-option error, and imported topics no longer get a category. This is a breaking change to the command-line interface that the PR description does not mention. Restore the option or document the removal.

Disqus import now fetches every thread live with no error handling and duplicates comments on re-run

Replacing PostCreator with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` makes the import fetch each thread's live URL with `open(url).read`. There is no timeout, no rescue, and no per-thread handling, so one 404 or network error aborts the import midway. The `ensure` block restores settings, but earlier threads are already imported. Re-running the import also appends every comment again: `import` returns the existing post, and the loop keeps creating posts for it. Rescue per thread, and skip comment creation when the topic already existed.

New gems are added for both Rails modes, but only the Rails 4 lockfile is updated

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally, and Rails 3 mode uses the same Gemfile with the default `Gemfile.lock`. Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this PR. In Rails 3 mode, `bundle install --deployment` or `--frozen` will fail because the lockfile is missing these gems. Update the Rails 3 lockfile too, or gate the gems by mode.

Test named 'is 404' asserts only failure, and no test renders the view

The example is titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' but only checks `should_not be_success`. It passes because the `ensure_embeddable` filter raises first when embeddable_host is unset, so `params.require` is never exercised. No spec renders the `best` or `loading` templates (no `render_views`), so a broken template like the one in best.html.erb:6 goes undetected. Add a request spec that checks the status code and renders the templates.

Every TopicRetriever example stubs the method under test, leaving the throttle and feed logic untested

Each example in the 'with a valid host' context stubs `retrieved_recently?` or `perform_retrieve`. The Redis throttle, the feed-first branch in `perform_retrieve` (topic_retriever.rb:40-43), the existing-embed early return, and `fetch_http` are never exercised. The most important behavior, that a second request within 60 seconds does not fetch again, has no coverage. Add examples that use a real or mock Redis and exercise `perform_retrieve` directly.

PollFeed import logic has no test coverage, only the gating conditions

The spec only checks when `poll_feed` is called and stubs `poll_feed` in the delegation example. The actual import path, including URL filtering, nil title or content handling, the `TopicEmbed.import` call per item, and the error behavior, is untested. That is the riskiest code in the feature (see the XSS and per-item abort findings above). Add examples that feed a sample RSS document through `poll_feed`.

String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1 or later

`String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1. If this application still targets Ruby 2.0 (as Discourse did in late 2013), every poll that reaches this line raises NoMethodError. Confirm the supported Ruby version, or use an encoding-safe alternative.

cook_method is accepted from any opts hash and can bypass sanitization

Downsize loop ignores failures and never verifies the final size before uploading

Each pass scales both dimensions by 0.8 (pixel count by 0.64), so five passes leave about 11% of the original pixels, which is not enough for a large original. Each loop iteration runs a full convert pass, and convert_with also runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! on the output, so an oversized upload can cost five decode/encode cycles plus five optimizer runs. If a pass fails partway (disk full, process killed, ImageMagick error during write), the file is left truncated or corrupt. Because the return value is ignored (see the loop above), the damaged file is then passed to Upload.create_for. updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) runs on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache call. It touches every selected calendar for the credential, across all event types, to bump updatedAt. Line 142 computes `end` from slotStartTime, so `end` always equals `start`. The end-of-day comparison therefore tests the slot start against workingHour.endTime, not the slot end. A slot starting at 16:30 that runs to 17:15 with working hours ending at 17:00 passes. For a round-robin event this means a fixed host can be offered slots that run past their working hours, which is the availability problem this PR is meant to fix. The end should be computed from slotEndTime.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: calculating the end time using `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

Zero-length override check compares Dayjs objects with === and never fires

`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. The branch meant to handle zero-length (start equals end) overrides is dead code. Such an override then falls through to the overlap comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override start is treated as inside the override and returned as available (line 133). Use .isSame(...) instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: comparing two `dayjs` objects using `===` checks object reference equality rather than value equality, which will always evaluate to false. Both recommend using `.isSame()` instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings

In checkIfIsAvailable, once a slot falls inside a date override, the function returns true at line 134 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at line 153. The busy array holds the host's existing Cal bookings and calendar events. For any fixed or round-robin host with a date override covering the slot, a booking or external calendar event at that time is ignored and the slot is still offered. Before this PR the busy check always ran for fixed hosts, so this is a regression that can produce double bookings on exactly the days that have date overrides. The override should only decide the working-hours question; the slot should still fall through to the busy check.

Working-hours check rejects slots that fall in a second same-day range

workingHours.find(...) returns truthy as soon as any entry for the weekday does not contain the slot (the if at line 143 returns true for any entry where the slot is before its start or after its end). Users commonly have several availability rows for one weekday (split shifts such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or a lunch break). A 14:00 slot is then rejected because the 09:00-12:00 entry does not contain it. This affects fixed hosts in individual events and fixed/round-robin hosts in team events, and removes roughly half of a split-shift user's slots. The logic should be: reject only if no entry for that day contains the slot. Also, a weekday with no entries (a day off) passes this check unchecked because find never matches, so the check does not enforce the intent stated in its comment.

Two date-override ranges on the same day make every slot on that day unavailable

dateOverrides.find(...) returns true for the first same-day override that does not contain the slot (the returns at lines 115, 121 and 124). The outer check then treats this as 'slot is outside the override' and returns false at line 130. The predicate never asks whether some other override on that day contains the slot. With two override rows for one date, for example 14:00-15:00 and 16:00-17:00 (the data model allows multiple date-override rows per date), a 14:00 slot is rejected because the 16:00 override does not contain it, and a 16:00 slot is rejected because the 14:00 override does not contain it. All slots on that day disappear for that host. The check should be whether some same-day override contains the slot (some, not find-with-rejection).

Override day matching mixes server-local and UTC dates and can attach an override to the wrong day

The override's day is computed as dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD'). dayjs(date.start) is in the server process's local timezone, while the slot side, slotStartTime.format(...), is in UTC (time.utc()). On a server whose TZ is not UTC the two sides use different calendars, so the override may match the wrong day or none. Separately, the day is taken from the UTC date of the shifted instant rather than the organizer's local date. An override at 02:00 on 22 Jan in Asia/Kolkata becomes 20:30Z on 21 Jan, so it also rejects the organizer's daytime 21 Jan slots (for example 09:30 IST), which have no override. Day matching should be done on organizer-local dates for both the override and the slot.

Override UTC offset is taken at the wall-clock-as-UTC instant, so it is off by an hour on DST-change days

Overrides are stored as organizer wall-clock time encoded as UTC. The offset is computed with dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone) at that encoded instant, which can differ from the real instant by up to 14 hours. When the encoded instant and the real instant fall on opposite sides of a DST transition, the wrong offset is used. Example: America/New_York override at 03:30 on 2023-03-12 (already on EDT). The encoded instant 03:30Z is before the 07:00Z switch, so offset -5 is used, and the bound becomes 08:30Z instead of 07:30Z. The same pattern is used in packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213, so the lib and the trpc check share the error.

packages/types/schedule.d.ts now declares TimeRange.timeZone as optional, and this code passes override.timeZone straight into .tz(...) with no guard. If a caller omits it, dayjs falls back to the process's local timezone with no error. Offsets are then computed for the server's zone rather than the organizer's, and slots are shifted silently. The caller contract should be made explicit (required parameter, or an explicit guard and fallback).

The only new test is a second timezone assertion on a single-user event with hosts: []. Nothing covers the headline fix, a round-robin event where a fixed host has a date override, so the fixed-host path in getSchedule is never exercised with overrides. Nothing covers busy bookings or calendar events that fall inside a date override (which would catch the busy-check bypass). Nothing covers two override rows on the same date, or split same-day working hours, or a slot that runs past the end of working hours. The existing suite therefore passes with all of these defects present. Tests for each of these should be added.

Class Javadoc claims this is an unchanged 4.8.3 fixture

The Javadoc says this is the Keycloak 4.8.3 implementation and that future versions should work without any change to this provider. This PR adds recovery-code support to the class, a credential type 4.8.3 never had. The comment is now wrong, and the class no longer serves as a frozen 4.8.3 compatibility baseline.

Switching to user storage leaves stale local recovery-code credentials

When updateCredential succeeds, the local recovery-codes credential is not removed. getCredential then prefers the federated credential, so any previously created local set becomes unreachable for authentication, but it remains in the local store and in stored-credential listings. Regenerating codes after user storage starts supporting the type leaves duplicate, dead recovery credentials.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

false_positives.candidate:
Null-strategy variants run without the rolling-updates feature that the docs say is required

createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, so the rolling-updates feature is only enabled for the RECREATE variant. The operator docs changed in this PR state that while the feature is in preview 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' Under that statement, the testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null cases exercise a configuration the docs call invalid, and they still expect rolling/recreate upgrade status. Either the early return should also enable the feature, or the docs claim is wrong and should say the requirement applies only when an update strategy is set.

setEnabledFeatures replaces the whole enabled-features list with an immutable List.of

The call overwrites any enabled features already set on the FeatureSpec returned by getTestKeycloakDeployment, rather than adding rolling-updates to them, so any feature the base deployment enables is silently dropped for these test cases. Because List.of is immutable, any later code that appends to getEnabledFeatures() on this spec would throw UnsupportedOperationException. Merging into a mutable list would avoid both problems.

Changed and new exit codes (3 and 4) are a documented contract but no test asserts them

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 is added. The update-compatibility guide presents these exit codes as the interface for CI/DevOps automation. However, UpdateCommandDistTest only checks exit code 0 (testCompatible), and testWrongVersions, which produces the recreate outcome, never asserts the exit code is 3. testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert 4 either. A regression in either code would not be caught, and the renumbering from 4 to 3 is a behavior change that the PR description does not call out.

Feature-disabled path is only tested for the metadata subcommand

testFeatureNotEnabled launches only UpdateCompatibility and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The equivalent feature gate added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck has no test, so a regression there (for example, the check command running without the feature) would not be caught. The test also asserts only the message, not the exit code 4 that the docs promise.

Exit code 4 is documented as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible', which misdescribes a precondition failure

Exit code 4 is returned when the rolling-updates feature is disabled and the tool never evaluates the upgrade at all. Describing it as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' tells automation that the upgrade was assessed and found incompatible. A script that branches on 3 versus 4 could then misread a misconfigured invocation as a real compatibility result. The row should say the command could not run because the feature is disabled.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removal listener gated on the V1 flag; V2-only deployments lose cleanup silently

The whole listener (role, client and group removal cleanup) is now wrapped in Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 flag, while the calls it makes dispatch to MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. With only V2 enabled, deleting a client, group or role no longer runs any cleanup. Nothing replaces it: ClientPermissionsV2 has no removal path, so the per-client admin-permissions resource (named by the client UUID) and its attached policies stay behind. The gate is not mentioned in the PR description. The gate should follow the flag that governs the active evaluator, and V2 cleanup should be implemented rather than suppressed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same incorrect V1 feature-flag guard on the AdminPermissions removal listener, which prevents cleanup in V2-only deployments and leaves orphaned permissions. The candidate's additional implementation details do not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission returns the literal 'Clients' and omits type-level grants

findByType(server, 'Clients', ...) also returns the all-clients resource itself, since its name and type are both 'Clients' (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init). If the caller holds the scope on it, the string 'Clients' is added to the result as if it were a client id. Clients covered only by a type-level grant are never added, because only per-client resources are inspected, whereas hasPermission(client, ...) falls back to the type-level resource. The result therefore disagrees with canView/canManage for the same caller.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the core bug: getClientsWithPermission includes the type-level resource's literal name 'Clients' as though it were a client ID. Although its claim that per-client resources are inspected is inconsistent with the golden comment, it still flags the same incorrect resource selection and invalid client identifier.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
init() never backfills the Clients resource type or new scopes for existing realms

init() returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms set up with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change never receive the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource, and nothing else backfills them. For such realms, creating a CLIENTS permission hits 'No scopes found.' (line 108), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, ...) passes a null resource into findByResource (ClientPermissionsV2 line 219) whenever no per-client resource exists. That will fail with an NPE or wrong result on client checks. No migration or test covers this path.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission passing a null resource into findByResource and causing a potential NullPointerException, matching the golden issue. It additionally explains a missing-backfill scenario that can produce the null resource.

false_positives.candidate:
canView(client) ignores per-client policies when the caller has type-level VIEW

canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() is true, and canView() is true for any caller holding VIEW on the all-'Clients' resource. In that case the per-client resource is never evaluated, so a negative or otherwise non-matching per-client VIEW permission is silently ignored and the client stays visible and listable. canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, ...) treat an existing per-client resource as overriding the type-level grant, and the users tests (testViewUserPermission) establish that per-object deny overrides the all-users VIEW grant. This method is inconsistent with that and lets an explicit deny be bypassed. No test covers a per-client deny on top of an all-clients VIEW grant.

setPermissionsEnabled throws, so the ClientRemovedEvent listener fails client deletion under V2

Before this PR MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited clients() from MgmtPermissions, so setPermissionsEnabled worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, and management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. When the listener is active (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled alongside V2), deleting any client throws during event dispatch and the deletion request fails.

V2 branch of the 4-arg evaluator() drops the target realm

In the V2 branch, evaluator(session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) calls new MgmtPermissionsV2(session, adminsRealm, admin) and never passes realm, although MgmtPermissionsV2 has a 4-argument constructor (session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) that carries it. The V1 branch passes realm. This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() build ClientPermissionsV2 from the realm field. Client permission checks made through this factory may therefore be evaluated against the admin's realm rather than the target realm, depending on what the 3-argument constructor assigns to realm.

Type-level grant is ignored when a per-client resource exists, contradicting the documented 'also if' contract

hasPermission(client, scope) consults the all-'Clients' resource only when no per-client resource exists. If a per-client resource exists (for example because some other client-specific permission was created), only that resource's policies are evaluated. A caller with MANAGE on all clients is then denied canManage(X) for such a client. The interface Javadoc added in this PR (ClientPermissionEvaluator) says canManage, canView, canConfigure and canMap* are also true for the 'all clients' permission, which this does not honor. Either the documentation or the precedence rule must change. canView(client) applies the opposite precedence, so the two methods disagree.

Inherited permission methods now throw UnsupportedOperationException on reachable paths

canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the mapRoles/manage/configure/view permission factories, resource(), getPermissions(), isPermissionsEnabled() and setPermissionsEnabled() all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Previously clients() under V2 returned the inherited V1 implementation. These are methods of the public evaluator interface that existing code calls (for example the legacy token-exchange check calls canExchangeTo, and client management-permission endpoints call getPermissions/resource). A request that reaches them now fails with HTTP 500 instead of a denial or a valid response. Nothing in the PR shows that callers are guarded.

getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources get no readable name

getResourceName special-cases USERS to return the username. There is no CLIENTS branch, so client resources fall back to resource.getDisplayName(). getOrCreateResource never sets a display name for client resources, so the name shown for a client permission would be null or the internal UUID rather than the clientId. The PR adds no mapping and no test for it.

void require* methods documented as 'Returns true'

requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() are void methods, but their Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if ...'. They should say they throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* method returns false, as the other require* methods in this interface do.

canView(client) repeats full policy evaluations for every client in a listing

canView(client) first calls canView(), which evaluates the all-clients resource, then canConfigure(client), which evaluates canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE), and finally hasPermission(client, VIEW). Each hasPermission call does a resource lookup and a full evaluatePermission. Checking each client in a list therefore costs several policy evaluations per client, and the type-level evaluation is repeated N times. Nothing caches the type-level result.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider, not BouncyCastle

The method builds a new, uninitialized KeyStore of the default type and returns its Provider, which is normally the JDK's SUN provider. Callers of getBouncyCastleProvider() that expect BouncyCastle, for example to look up algorithms by provider name, get the JDK provider silently. The method also allocates a throwaway KeyStore on every call. It should either return a real BC provider or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle.

true_positives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead ASN1Encoder calls whose results are discarded

Lines 114 and 115 create ASN1Encoder instances and discard the result. The returned DER sequence on lines 117-121 recomputes the same encodings. The dead calls look like a leftover and make the method harder to read.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify redundant ASN1Encoder operations whose results are discarded, while new instances in the return statement perform the actual encoding.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations

order() is added to the public CryptoProvider interface without a default implementation. Any existing implementation that does not override it, including out-of-tree providers, is not broken at compile time but throws AbstractMethodError. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls order() on every discovered provider, so such a provider fails during crypto initialization. A default method, for example returning 0, would keep existing implementations working.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same backward-compatibility issue: adding abstract order() to CryptoProvider breaks existing implementations that do not implement it. The candidate adds runtime failure details and a default-method mitigation.

false_positives.candidate:
Providers with equal order() are picked by classpath order, silently

detectProvider no longer rejects multiple providers. It stable-sorts by order() and takes the first entry. DefaultCryptoProvider (line 84), WildFlyElytronProvider (line 77) and FIPS1402Provider (line 115) all return 200. When two of them are on the same classpath, the winner is whichever ServiceLoader discovered first. Before this PR that case threw IllegalStateException; now it only logs at debug level. In a FIPS deployment that also has the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider on the classpath, the non-FIPS provider can be chosen with no error. Ties need a deterministic rule (for example, FIPS ranked above default) or should still fail. No test covers this selection logic.

Non-selected providers are constructed, and their constructors mutate global JVM security state

The ServiceLoader stream is collected into a list before sorting, so every discovered CryptoProvider constructor runs, including those that will not be selected. FIPS1402Provider's constructor (FIPS1402Provider.java line 94) inserts a KeycloakFipsSecurityProvider at JVM security slot 1. When BCFIPS is absent it also inserts BCFIPS and BCJSSE and rewrites the ssl.KeyManagerFactory/TrustManagerFactory properties. DefaultCryptoProvider's constructor registers a non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider with Security.addProvider. Previously these side effects were followed by a hard failure when more than one provider was present. Now the multi-provider case succeeds, so the side effects persist in a JVM that runs a different provider. Discovery should avoid constructing unselected providers, for example by ranking on metadata before instantiation.

AuthzClient.create() can pin the process-wide crypto provider to the minimal one

CryptoIntegration.init is process-global and effectively runs once, using the class loader of AuthzClient. If that loader cannot see the full crypto provider (for example, when the real crypto jar is in another class loader, such as an application server module), or if an application creates an AuthzClient before anything else initializes crypto, the global provider becomes AuthzClientCryptoProvider. Because init is a no-op afterwards, later code that needs the real provider keeps getting AuthzClientCryptoProvider, and most of its methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Before this change AuthzClient did not touch the global provider. Consider not installing a placeholder provider globally from this entry point.

Most provider methods throw a 'Not supported yet.' placeholder

About 17 methods, including getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory and wrapFactoryForTruststore, throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported yet.'). That is leftover IDE template text, and it suggests the feature is planned. Because this provider is now a global ServiceLoader entry, callers that reach it through CryptoIntegration.getProvider() get an opaque failure. The message should say the provider is limited to ECDSA conversion, or the methods should be implemented.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate signature length

The method copies signature[len..2*len) without checking signature.length. A short or malformed signature triggers an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than an IOException or a clean verification failure. The method is copied from the BC implementation but is new code here, so it should check that signature.length equals signLength.

Test only checks the module's own encoder and decoder round-trip

The assertion compares the concatenated R||S produced by asn1derToConcatenatedRS with the value obtained after encoding and decoding it again, using the same class. If both directions share a defect, or if the produced DER is not accepted by a standard verifier, the test still passes. The test should verify the DER output from concatenatedRSToASN1DER with java.security.Signature.verify, or check it against a known test vector.

ES384 and ES512 are tested with a P-256 key, so the real component sizes are not exercised

A single default EC key pair is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512, so ES384 and ES512 sign with P-256 keys. The 48-byte and 66-byte component paths are not tested with matching curves. The P-521 case matters most: R can be 66 bytes plus a sign byte, which hits the truncation branch in integerToBytes, and that path is never exercised. The test therefore gives false confidence for ES384 and ES512. Each algorithm should be tested with its own curve, P-384 and P-521.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deleted group silently reports a null subgroup count

The NPE is replaced by returning null from a method whose contract is a count. The missing group is swallowed here and the null propagates into representations (populateSubGroupCount assigns it directly). Callers that unbox the Long or compare it will now throw NPE far from the cause. Other methods in this adapter throw IllegalStateException('Not found in database') when the group is gone, so behavior is inconsistent. Pick one defined behavior and document it on GroupModel.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same issue: getSubGroupsCount() returns null for a missing group, violating its non-null count contract and risking NPEs in callers that unbox or compare the result.

true_positives.golden_comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reader thread is not joined, so late failures are ignored

deletedAll is set and the assertion runs at line 157 without joining the reader thread started at line 139. The reader may still be inside an in-flight request, and any exception it records after the assertion is evaluated is never checked. The test can therefore pass despite the failure it is meant to catch. The thread should be joined, with a timeout, before asserting.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race: the test sets deletedAll and asserts without waiting for the reader thread, allowing exceptions recorded afterward to go unchecked.

false_positives.candidate:
Paged subgroup listing still dereferences a possibly-null model

getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) calls modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. The supplier resolves to null when another request has deleted the group, which is the race this PR targets, so this still throws the same NPE. The same unguarded pattern appears at lines 262 and 268 in the other two paged overloads. Only getSubGroupsCount was guarded, so the reported bug is only partly fixed.

Null guard in getRoleMappings tests the supplier instead of the group

The check 'if (group == null)' tests the Supplier<GroupModel> parameter. GroupAdapter always passes its non-null modelSupplier, so the guard never fires. When the underlying group has been deleted, the supplier returns null, and that null reaches the lazy loader. The comment describes exactly the case this guard was meant to handle, so the intended protection is missing and the PR does not address it. The check should be on group.get() == null before calling the loader.

getAttributes and getSubGroups have no null handling for a deleted group

Unlike getRoleMappings, getAttributes (lines 66-68) and getSubGroups (lines 90-92) pass the supplier straight to DefaultLazyLoader. The loaders at lines 55 and 57 dereference the source (source.getAttributes(), source.getSubGroupsStream()). Assuming the loader runs on the supplied source when the value is not yet loaded, a group deleted before its first attribute or subgroup access makes the supplier return null and the loader throws NPE. That affects getFirstAttribute, getAttributes, getAttributeStream and getSubGroupsStream() in GroupAdapter, so the concurrent NPE remains reachable.

Parent lookup result used without a null check during hierarchy build

session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId()) returns null if the parent was deleted between listing and this lookup. parentModel is then passed to groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel) at line 51 (when admin permissions are off), to toRepresentation inside computeIfAbsent at line 57, and to populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent) at line 60, which calls getSubGroupsCount() on null. This is the same concurrent-deletion NPE in the group listing path, and the PR edits this file without handling it. A null check that drops the orphaned child or skips the parent is needed.

Exception during deletion leaves a non-daemon busy-looping thread running

If group(...).remove() at line 153 throws (for example a 500 from the bug under test), the exception escapes the forEach and deletedAll.set(true) at line 155 never runs. The reader thread (lines 139-149) then loops forever issuing HTTP requests. As a non-daemon thread it also keeps the JVM alive, so the run hangs instead of failing cleanly. The flag should be set in a finally block, and the reader should be a daemon or be stopped explicitly.

Race-based test may not reproduce the NPE and has no deterministic interleaving

The NPE requires a cached adapter with a loaded group, a concurrent deletion, and then a lazy access. This test depends on timing between one reader thread and 100 sequential deletes, and it only asserts that no exception reached the client. Nothing shows it fails on the base commit, so it may pass without the fix. The author should confirm it reproduces the failure without the change, or drive the interleaving deterministically (for example by deleting the group on the server between the read and the access).

Reader thread spins on HTTP requests with no pause

The reader loop at lines 139-149 issues back-to-back list requests over 100 groups for the whole deletion phase with no sleep or backoff. This saturates the shared test server, slows the test, and adds load that can cause timeouts on CI. A short pause between iterations would avoid this.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation

The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in this change is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java, and no no-arg overload exists in the class hierarchy. The `services` module will not compile, so the whole PR (including all the new tests) cannot build or run. The intended call is presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which is already non-null inside this branch.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same issue: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel argument. The candidate additionally explains the compilation failure caused by the missing argument.

false_positives.candidate:
Re-auth skip is disabled for every user whenever passkeys are enabled in the realm

The shortcut that skips the username form during re-authentication is now bypassed for any user as soon as passkeys are enabled for the realm, regardless of whether that particular user has a passkey. A password-only user re-authenticating with prompt=login in a passkey-enabled realm is now shown the username page and must submit it, where previously they were skipped. The only new UsernameForm re-auth test uses a passkey-only user, so this regression for password-only users is not covered. If the intent is to only show the form when the user can use a passkey, the condition should check the user's passkey credentials rather than only the realm flag.

Negative webauthn-button check uses catch(Exception), so it can pass vacuously

In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (and again around line 312), the absence of the webauthn form is checked with `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any Exception thrown while looking up the element, such as a WebDriverException from a stale or not-yet-loaded page, is swallowed and the check passes without verifying anything. The same PR and file already use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` for this kind of check, which only accepts the expected exception.

Unused import NoSuchElementException left behind

The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` uses were replaced by `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)` in this PR, so the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is now unused. This can fail a checkstyle or unused-import check in the build.

Unused PasswordCredentialModel import added by this PR

The import `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` is added in this PR, but nothing in the file references it (the new tests only use string/nullValue checks). It should be removed to keep the build's unused-import checks clean.

false_negatives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offset is passed straight into a queryset slice, which Django rejects

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is the raw negative offset and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices and raises an error, so the request returns a 500. The branch that is supposed to reach data beyond normal pagination bounds therefore never returns data. A user can reach this with any crafted cursor string whose offset is negative, provided the advanced flag is set.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: a negative cursor offset is used to slice a Django QuerySet, which does not support negative indices and raises an AssertionError. The candidate adds trigger conditions and consequences without changing the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member is dereferenced without a None check

RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional, since a requester may not be a member of the organization. The expression `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` only avoids the dereference when the user is a superuser. For any other requester with no membership record, this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Whether OrganizationAuditPermission guarantees membership for non-superusers is not visible in this diff, so this needs a None guard or a confirmed invariant.

Two concurrent cold Search or watch-event calls for the same namespace now build two full indexes in parallel, roughly doubling memory and CPU. Previously these failures only surfaced as errors on the first gRPC call and never stopped construction. By the design (the finally block completes the failed offset 100), both offsets 100 and 101 complete, so a later commit should reach 102.
